solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Limited outlet for courage and audacity

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is informal for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: Somewhere to vent one's courage and nerve turns out to be restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE (British slang for courage, as in 'lose your bottle') plus NECK (cheek, audacity).
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow passage restricting flow, as at the top of a container, is a limited outlet.

clue.text: 36″ statue?

definitions.meaning: a chest measurement of thirty-six inches, the figure a dressmaker records
a sculpture of the head and shoulders, the question mark admitting it is only part of a statue

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a woman's chest size; the other is a sculpted head and shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a chest measurement and a carved head-and-shoulders sculpture.

clue.text: Sailor man covered by waterproof

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
Paul is a man's name
to be in something, such as a coat, is to be covered by it

explanation.surface: A sailor keeps dry under oilskins.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself an old word for a sailor, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy waterproof sheet of tarred canvas, used as a noun for any such cover.

clue.text: Heard northerners slip

indicators.note: heard says the word for these people is to be judged by its sound

parts.note: the Lapps are people of the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: People from the north are said to have stumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error or failure, a momentary lapse of attention.

clue.text: Fully in order to cancel

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complete instruction given in order to annul something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as a phrase with 'to', but 'in' is fodder and 'order' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel something is to make it void, of no legal force.

clue.text: Investigator found nothing in awkward position

indicators.note: in says the one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in an awkward position
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A detective discovers no clue, leaving them in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This official investigates sudden or suspicious deaths, holding inquests.

clue.text: Develop arts to obtain spun swaddling lace

indicators.note: spun says the run of letters found is turned round and read backwards
swaddling means wrapping up, so the clue words wrap the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Advice to grow artistic skills by acquiring twisted lace for wrapping a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop' looks like the definition, but its last letter starts the run: PARTSTOOB sits inside 'develoP ARTS TO OBtain', and 'spun' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap or loop on a boot, used like a lace to pull it on, a loose sense of lace.

clue.text: Not in the same beat

parts.note: someone not in is out
do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Someone out of step with the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival is to surpass or outdo them.

clue.text: Do what is expected at start of race

definitions.meaning: to conform and obey the rules
runners literally place their feet on the start mark before a race

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for conforming comes from runners lining up at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for conforming, literally what sprinters do at the starting mark.

clue.text: To some extent at home before a hearing perhaps

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: in means at home
hearing is one example of a sense

explanation.surface: Staying in ahead of a court hearing, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says hearing is just one example of SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A set phrase meaning partly, in some respects, to a limited degree.

clue.text: See 6
Holding it should improve one's prospects

definitions.text: Holding it should improve one's prospects

parts.words: Holding it should improve one's prospects
parts.note: prospects is taken literally as what one sees: an eyeglass on a handle, held up to the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: 'prospects' suggests career chances, but here it means the view; the item is a pair of spectacles held on a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of glasses on a long handle, held to the eyes to see better.

clue.text: Lady stopped short in front of a new plant

indicators.note: in front of places the cut name ahead of the following pieces
stopped short says the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Valerie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman halted before a fresh specimen of greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering herb whose root is used as a sedative.

clue.text: Laziness of large number in shorthand

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SH is the shortened written form of shorthand
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: Idleness shown by many in a typing pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is one of the seven deadly sins, idleness or indolence.

clue.text: Ours is a minor planet it is sometimes said

definitions.text: Ours is a minor planet it is sometimes said

parts.words: Ours is a minor planet it is sometimes said
parts.note: a common saying when meeting an acquaintance by chance far from home, recast as astronomy

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'It's a … !' on chance meetings is presented as if describing Earth's size.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation used on meeting someone unexpectedly, that the planet is little.

clue.text: 'My meal's served… Wine!'

indicators.note: served suggests dishing up, so these letters are presented in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner calls for a drink once the food arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fortified wine from Madeira.

clue.text: Dog's leash may be twisted

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the dog

indicators.note: twisted says these letters are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog's lead may get tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of small Welsh terrier.

clue.text: Urban development that's novel in authentic setting

indicators.note: setting means the second word forms the surround for the first

parts.note: authentic means real
novel means new

explanation.surface: A housing scheme that is innovative in a genuine way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Regeneration of run-down city areas, as in urban renewal schemes.

clue.text: Resist having support

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with money
a stand is a support

explanation.surface: Refusing to give way when one has backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand an attack is to resist it successfully.

clue.text: Connection leaking terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A joint that leaks badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A link or coupling, as in a mechanical linkage.

clue.text: Learn about old prince with new role

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: new says the following word is formed afresh

explanation.surface: Finding out about a former royal taking on a fresh part.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore a subject is to investigate and learn about it.

clue.text: Not taken in by consumers

parts.note: reads as shoppers not being fooled, but means food that eaters did not swallow

explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests deceived and 'consumers' suggests shoppers; literally it is food left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left on the plate has not been eaten, taken in by those consuming.

clue.text: Maybe Sam has a recipe that's ambiguous

parts.note: Uncle Sam, the personification of the USA, so Sam might be an uncle
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone called Sam owns cooking instructions that are vague.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the old prescription abbreviation (℞).
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiguous means open to more than one reading, so not clear.

clue.text: Tired but cautious going round the point

indicators.note: going round says the first word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: wary means cautious
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Exhausted yet careful as one turns a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary is a synonym of tired or fatigued.

clue.text: Partially gag growing hostility…

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A joke that slowly turns into antagonism.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggressive behaviour or hostile trouble-making.

clue.text: Fighting opponent

parts.note: reads as a combatant one faces, but means a person opposed to fighting

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is a rival in a bout; the real one is someone against war.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes violence and war on principle.

clue.text: …as wife's taking concealed holiday in Italy

indicators.note: concealed says the letters are held inside these clue words

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a wife sneaks off on a break abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a feast day or festival.

clue.text: Ignoble purpose

definitions.meaning: to have in mind or intend, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Mean covers both base or petty behaviour and to intend something.

clue.text: Equip mother taking part in rambling discourse

indicators.note: taking places the following piece alongside the mother

parts.note: to rig is to equip, as a ship
ma is mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Kitting out mum, who plays a role in a long-winded speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, confused and pointless account or procedure.

clue.text: Opening for actor

parts.note: reads as a job opportunity for a performer, but is a literal entrance used by theatre staff

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a role going; it is a physical door at the back of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre's back entrance used by performers and staff.

clue.text: See 28
Agreed barn could be built — scene of uproar

indicators.note: could be built suggests construction from parts, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Permission given for a farm building, and chaos follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a place for bear-baiting, now any rowdy, noisy place.
